items.reasons: The view is mixed. The screen and red marquee are drawn as a flat front elevation, but the seat and wheel are seen from above. The cabinet has no lit top plane, so the cabinet and seat do not read as one 3/4 object.
Only a 1-px dark strip shows as a top, so this is a flat front elevation of a wall display. In the room it overlaps the bottom of the back wall instead of standing on the floor.
The blue garments merge into one muddy lump with a bright blue sticker shirt in the middle. The single chrome pole and round base read as a table or lamp, not a clothing rack.
The microwave and rice cooker are flat front elevations with only a 1–2 row top strip. The rack is one tile wide and looks undersized next to the originals' furniture.
The thin white frame is drawn as a front elevation with no visible top plane. The legs look like table legs, and the clothes hang as flat stickers with thin noisy frame lines.
The white work surface reads as a lit top plane, and the monitor sits on the cart. The outline and palette match the originals, and the bottles and dials are clean.
It is a 1-tile-wide, 3-tile-tall strip with no top plane, which is neither a 3/4 view nor a front view of a folding screen. At 1x and in the room it reads as a pillar or pole, not a curtain screen.
The gray spindle, white blocks and the orange panel with bright pixels form a busy jumble. There is no clear bed, chuck or tailstock, so it reads as a generic machine rather than a lathe.
The tap tower is a tall, thin white hook shape, and the beer glass hangs beside it rather than sitting clearly on the drip tray. At 1x it is an illegible sliver.
The kasagi is seen from above as a dark plank, with red nuki, red pillars and stone bases resting on the floor. The outline and shading match the chipset.
The white lid reads as a top plane, with a control panel and paper trays below. It is clean and correctly scaled in the room.
The desktops are lit planes seen from above, with partitions, green lamps and legs touching the floor. The wood palette matches the wardrobe original.
The top is only a thin gray line, so this is a flat front elevation, unlike the cooler original's clear top plane. The separate base strip below has gapped feet that look detached.
The blue canopy top reads from above and the open shelves show dairy packs. The outline and scale match the cooler original.
The top plane shows stocked items from above, with three clean shelves of bottles. It sits on the floor at the right scale.
Same clean 3/4 construction as the detergent gondola: boxes on the top plane and bottle rows on the shelves. The scale fits.
The wide lit wooden top plane sits over shelves of bottles. The palette and outline match the wardrobe original.
The panel is a flat front elevation with no top rail plane. The diamond mesh is noisy and high-contrast against the tan fill. Inside a room it reads as a crate rather than a fence segment.
The gray roof plane is visible from above above the front face with its door and exit sign. The ground line is clean and the scale fits a door.
There is no locker door or frame detail; it is an open gray box with a diagonal broom and a red dustpan blob. At 1x it reads as a sliver with a red smear.
